In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾ ﴿and when the stars scatter﴾ ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾ ﴿and when the graves are overturned﴾ ﴿a soul will know what it has sent forward and what it has left behind﴾

Know that the meaning is that when these things, which are the signs of the Hour (ashrat al-sa'ah, the minor and major portents announcing the Last Day), occur, then resurrection and dispersal take place. In the interpretation of these verses there are several discussions.

The first: concerning the explanation of each of these things which are the signs of the Hour. There are four here: two of them relate to the heavenly realm (al-'ulwiyyat) and two relate to the lower realm (al-suflIyyat). The first is His saying: ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾, i.e., it is cleft, and it is like His saying: ﴿And the day when the sky will be split open with clouds﴾ [al-Furqan: 25], ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1], ﴿And when the sky is split open, and becomes red like rose-colored leather﴾ [al-Rahman: 37], ﴿And the sky is opened and becomes gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19], and ﴿the sky will be split by it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18]. Al-Khalil said: "This form (infatarat) does not come as a verb of the (feminine) pattern; rather it is like their saying: murdi' (nursing) and ha'id (menstruating), and if it were on the pattern of the verb it would be munfatirah, as He said: ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾." As for the second, His saying: ﴿and when the stars scatter﴾, the meaning is clear, because when the structure of the sky is dissolved, the stars must scatter onto the earth.

Know that we mentioned in some earlier surah that the philosophers deny the possibility of rending and rejoining in the spheres. Our proof for the possibility of this is that bodies are alike in being bodies, so whatever applies to one of them must be valid for the others. We say they are alike because it is valid to divide them into heavenly and earthly, and the basis of the division is common to both parts; so the heavenly and the lower things share in being bodies. We say that whenever this is so, what applies to the heavenly things must be valid for the lower things, because like things share one ruling; therefore whenever a ruling is valid for one of them, it must be valid for the rest.

صفحة ٧١
As for the two lower things: the first is His saying: ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾, and on it there are several interpretations:

One: some seas penetrate others when the barrier that Allah placed as a partition (barzakh) is removed, and then the whole becomes one sea. That barrier is removed due to the quaking and splitting of the earth.

Second: the waters of the seas are now still and gathered, and when they are burst forth they scatter and their water departs.

Third: al-Hasan said: "fujjirat" means "dried up."

Know that according to all three interpretations, the meaning is that the seas change from their original form and attribute. This is like the change of the earth from its attribute, as in His saying: ﴿On the day the earth will be changed into other than the earth﴾ [Ibrahim: 48], and the change of the mountains from their attribute, as in His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord will scatter them as dust, and leave it a level plain﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105-106].

Fourth: some read "fujirat" with light stress, and Mujahid read "fajarat" in the active voice with light stress, meaning "rebelled" (baghat), because the barrier had been removed, in consideration of His saying: ﴿they do not transgress [each other]﴾ [al-Rahman: 20], since al-baghy (transgression) and al-fujur (sinful deviation) are brothers.

As for the second: His saying: ﴿and when the graves are overturned﴾. Know that bu'thira and buhthira have the same meaning, and both are composed of al-ba'th and al-bahth with a raa' (r) added to them, and the meaning is that they are stirred up, and their bottom is turned to the top and their inside becomes outside. Then there are two possibilities here:

One: the graves are overturned in that those in them of the dead come out alive, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 2].

The second: they are overturned to bring out what is in their bellies of gold and silver, because among the signs of the Hour is that the earth will bring forth the cores of its liver of its gold and silver, and after that will be the emergence of the dead. The first is closer, because the indication of the graves for the first is more complete.

The second station: concerning the purpose of this order. Know that the aim of these verses is to show the destruction of the world and the annihilation of this life, and the ending of obligations. The sky is like a roof and the earth is like a building, and whoever wishes to ruin a house begins first by ruining the roof, and that is His saying: ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾. Then the destruction of the sky necessarily entails the scattering of the stars, and that is His saying: ﴿and when the stars scatter﴾. Then, after the destruction of the sky and the stars, He, exalted is He, destroys everything on the face of the earth, and that is His saying: ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾. Then, at the last of the matter, He, exalted is He, destroys the earth which is the building, and that is His saying: ﴿and when the graves are overturned﴾, for it is an indication of turning the earth upside down, its back to its belly and its belly to its back.

The third station: concerning the explanation of His saying: ﴿a soul will know what it has sent forward and what it has left behind﴾, and in it there are two possibilities.

The first: that the intended meaning of these matters is the mention of the Day of Resurrection. Then in it there are several interpretations:

One, which is the most correct: the purpose of it is a warning against disobedience and an encouragement to obedience, meaning that every person will know on this day what he sent forward, so he did not neglect it, and what he left behind, so he fell short in it, because His saying: ﴿what it sent forward﴾ implies an act, and ﴿left behind﴾ implies an omission; so this statement implies doing, omitting, falling short and fulfilling. If he sent forward the grave sins and left behind righteous deeds, then his abode is the Fire; and if he sent forward righteous deeds and left behind the grave sins, then his abode is Paradise.

Second: what it sent forward of deeds that brought them into existence, and what it left behind of a sunnah (a precedent) that those after it follow, whether good or evil.

Third: al-Dahhak said: "what it sent forward of obligations and what it left behind," meaning what it neglected.

Fourth: Abu Muslim said: "what it sent forward of deeds in the early part of its life and what it left behind in the final part of its life."

If it is asked: at which station of the stations of the Resurrection does this knowledge take place? We say: as for general knowledge, it takes place at the first moment of the gathering, because the obedient sees the traces of happiness and the disobedient sees the traces of wretchedness at the outset.

As for detailed knowledge, it takes place at the reading of the records and the reckoning.

صفحة ٧٢
The second possibility: that the intended meaning is that it is said: the rising of the Resurrection, rather at the appearance of the signs of the Hour and the ending of obligations, when deeds no longer benefit after that, as He said: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before, or earned good through its faith﴾ [al-An'am: 158]. Thus what a person did up to that limit is his first and last deeds, because he has no deed after that. This view was mentioned by al-Qaffal.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 82, verse 6–8 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ ﴿Who created you, then proportioned you, then made you balanced?﴾ ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.﴾

Know that when He, glorified is He, informed in the first verse of the occurrence of the Gathering and the Resurrection, He mentioned in this verse that which rationally indicates its possibility or its occurrence, and that is from two aspects:

The first: The Generous God, from whose generosity it is not permissible to cut off the tables of His bounties from the sinners, how is it permissible in His generosity that He not avenge the wronged against the wrongdoer?

The second: The Capable One who created this human structure and then proportioned it and balanced it, either it is said that He created it without wisdom or with wisdom. If He created it without wisdom, that would be purposeless, and that is not permissible for the Wise. And if He created it with wisdom, that wisdom is either returning to God, exalted is He, or to the servant. The first is invalid, because He, glorified is He, is exalted above perfecting Himself and benefiting. Thus the second is determined, namely that He created the creation for a wisdom returning to the servant, and that wisdom either manifests in this world or in an abode other than this world. The first is invalid, because this world is an abode of trial and testing, not an abode of benefit and recompense. And since all of that is invalid, it is established that after this abode there must be another abode. Thus it is established that acknowledging the existence of the Generous God, who is able to create, proportion and balance, obliges the rational person to be certain that He, glorified is He, will raise the dead and gather them, and that prevents them from acknowledging the non-occurrence of the Gathering and the Resurrection. And this argument is the very one mentioned in Surah al-Tin, where He said: (﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4] up to His saying: ﴿So what causes you, after this, to deny the Recompense?﴾ [al-Tin: 7]). This argument is suitable with the Arabs who used to affirm the Creator but deny the return, and it is also suitable with one who negates both the origination and the return together, because the balanced creation indicates the Creator, and through it indicates the soundness of the saying of the Gathering and the Resurrection.

If it is said: The basis of this argument is that He is Wise, and for that reason He said in Surah al-Tin after this argument: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin: 8], so it would have been required that He say in this surah: "What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Wise?"

The answer: The Generous must be Wise, because conveying a bounty to another, if it were not based on the motive of wisdom, would be squandering, not generosity. But if it is based on the motive of wisdom, then it is called generosity. If this is established, we say: His being Generous indicates the occurrence of the Gathering from two aspects as we have established; as for His being Wise, it indicates the occurrence of the Gathering from this second aspect. So the mention of the Generous here is more appropriate than the mention of the Wise. This is the complete discussion on the manner of the composition. Let us return to the exegesis.

As for His saying: (O man). There are two opinions: One of them: that it refers to the disbeliever, because of His saying after that: ﴿Nay, but you deny the Recompense﴾. ʿAṭāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Ibn al-Asad ibn Kalada ibn Usayd, because he struck the Prophet ﷺ and Allah did not punish him, and He revealed this verse.

The second opinion: that it encompasses all the disobedient, and this is closer to the truth, because the specificity of the cause does not undermine the generality of the wording. As for His saying: ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ the meaning is: what deceived you and embellished falsehood for you until you abandoned the obligations and committed the prohibitions. The meaning is: what made you feel secure from His punishment. It is said: "He deceived him about so-and-so" when he made him feel secure from a danger from that direction while it was not safe. It is like His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ [Luqman: 33]. This is if we take His saying "O man" to refer to all the disobedient. But if we take it to refer to the disbeliever, the meaning is: what moved you to disbelief and denial of the Messengers, and rejection of the Gathering and the Resurrection? Here there are questions:

The first: That His being Generous requires that man be deceived by His generosity, by evidence from reason and transmitted report. As for reason, generosity is the bestowal of what is fitting without compensation. Since the Truthful, exalted is He, is absolutely Generous, He does not seek compensation; and whenever this is so, the obedience of the obedient and the disobedience of the sinners are equal to Him, and this necessitates deception, because it is far-fetched that the Rich would inflict pain upon the weak without any benefit at all. As for transmitted report, what is related from ʿAlī, peace be upon him, that he called his servant several times and he did not answer him; he looked and found him at the door, and said to him: "Why did you not answer me?" He said: "Because of my confidence in your forbearance and my security from your punishment." He admired his answer and freed him. And they also said: "Among the generosity of a man is the bad manners of his servants." Since it is established that his generosity requires deception by it, how then does He make it here a preventer from deception by it?

The answer is from several aspects:

First: The meaning of the verse is that when you saw God's forbearance toward His creation, you thought that this was because there is no reckoning and no abode except this abode. So what moved you to this deception, and emboldened you to deny the Gathering and the Resurrection? For your Lord is Generous; so, by His generosity, He does not hasten punishment, extending the period for repentance and delaying the recompense until He gathers the people in the abode He made for them for recompense. The sum is that the abandonment of hastening punishment is for the sake of generosity, and that does not require deception into thinking there is no abode after this abode.

Second: When His generosity reached the point where He does not withhold the tables of His kindness from the disobedient, then by avenging the wronged against the wrongdoer, it is more fitting. Thus His being Generous requires great fear from this consideration, and the abandonment of boldness and deception.

Third: Abundance of generosity necessitates striving and diligence in service, and shame before deception and negligence.

Fourth: Some people said: He only said "by your Lord, the Generous" so that it would be an answer to that question, so that one would say: "Your generosity deceived me, and had it not been for your generosity I would not have done it; for You saw and concealed, and You had power and gave respite." This answer is valid only if the intended meaning of His saying "O man" is not the disbeliever.

The second question: What have the exegetes mentioned regarding the cause of this deception? We say: there are several aspects:

First: Qatada said: the cause of the son of Adam's deception is Satan's enticement of him.

Second: al-Hasan said: his foolishness and ignorance deceived him.

Third: Muqatil said: the pardon of Allah toward him deceived him, when He did not punish him at the beginning of his affair. It was also said to al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad: "If Allah makes you stand on the Day of Resurrection and says to you: 'What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?' what will you say?" He said: "I will say: Your lowered veils deceived me."

The third question: What is the meaning of the reading of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, "mā aghharaka"? We say: it is either as an exclamation of wonder, or as an interrogation, from your saying "gharra al-rajul" (he became heedless), so he is "gharr" when he is heedless, and from your saying "bayyatahumu al-ʿaduww wa-hum gharrūn" (the enemy attacked them by night while they were heedless), and "aghharahu ghayruh" means he made him heedless. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who created you﴾, know that when He described Himself with generosity, He mentioned these three matters as an indication of the reality of that generosity.

The first of them: Creation, which is His saying: ﴿Who created you﴾. There is no doubt that this is generosity of existence, because existence is better than non-existence, and life is better than death. And He is the One who said: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ [al-Baqara: 28].

The second: His saying: "then proportioned you," meaning He made you whole, with all your limbs intact, hearing and seeing. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust, then from a drop, then proportioned you into a man?﴾ [al-Kahf: 37]. Dhu al-Nun said: "proportioned you" means He subjected to you all the existents entirely, and did not make you subjected to any of them; then He made your tongue speak the remembrance, your heart with reason, your spirit with knowledge, your inner self with faith, honored you with command and prohibition, and preferred you over many of those He created with a preference.

The third: His saying: "then made you balanced," and concerning it there are two discussions:

The first discussion: Muqatil said: He means He balanced your creation in the two eyes, the two ears, the two hands and the two feet, so He did not make one of the two hands longer, nor one of the two eyes wider. It is like His saying: ﴿Yes, We are able to even reshape his fingertips﴾ [al-Qiyama: 4]. Its explanation, as known in the science of anatomy, is that He, glorified is He, assembled the two sides of this body in equal proportion, so that there is no disparity between its two halves, neither in the bones, nor in their shapes, nor in their openings, nor in the veins, arteries, and nerves that run through them and emerge from them. The thorough discussion of this does not befit this science. ʿAṭāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: He made you upright, balanced, of good form, not like the bent beast. Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: He balanced your creation and brought you out in the best of stature, and by that balance He made you prepared to receive intellect, power and thought, and by that made you dominant over all animals and plants, and reaching through perfection that which none of the bodies of this world has reached.

The second discussion: The Kufans read "fa-ʿadalaka" with the lightened form, and concerning it there are several aspects:

First: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: the meaning may be that He turned some of your limbs toward others until they became balanced.

Second: al-Farrāʾ said: "fa-ʿaddalaka," i.e., He turned you into whatever form He willed. Then he said: the intensified form is the better of the two, because you say: "ʿaddaltuka ila kadha" just as you say "sarraftuka ila kadha," and it is not good to say "ʿadaltuka fīhi" nor "ṣaraftuka fīhi." So in the first reading, the "fī" in His saying "in whatever form" is a complement to the composition, which is good; and in the second reading he made it a complement to His saying "fa-ʿadalaka," which is weak. Know that the objection of the readers is directed only at this second aspect; as for the first aspect which Abu ʿAli al-Farisi mentioned, the objection does not apply.

Third: Al-Qaffal transmitted from some of them that they are two dialects with one meaning.

As for His saying: ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾, there are several discussions. The first: Is "mā" superfluous or not? There are two opinions: The first: that it is not superfluous, rather it has the meaning of condition and consequence, so the meaning is: in whatever form He willed to assemble you in it, He assembled you. On this view, Abu Salih and Muqatil said: the meaning is that if He willed, He assembled you in a form other than the human form, such as the form of a dog, a donkey, a pig, or a monkey.

The second opinion: that it is a confirmatory complement, and the meaning is: in whatever form of the different forms that His will and wisdom require, for He assembles you in its likeness. On this view, the verse admits several aspects:

First: that the intended meaning of the different forms is the resemblance to the father and mother, or the relatives of the father or the relatives of the mother, and the meaning is that He assembles you in the likeness of these people. This is supported by what is reported that he, peace be upon him, said concerning this verse: "When the drop settles in the womb, Allah brings before it every lineage between it and Adam."

The second: which is what al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjaj mentioned, that the intended meaning of the different forms is the difference according to height and shortness, beauty and ugliness, maleness and femaleness. The indication of this state of the capable Creator is most manifest, because the drop is a body of uniform parts, and the influence of the nature of the two parents upon it is equal; the active agent acting by nature upon a uniform receptive matter produces only one act. So when the effects and attributes differ, that difference indicates that the governor is the capable, choosing One. Al-Qaffal said:

The variety of creatures and colours is like the variety of conditions in wealth and poverty, health and sickness. Just as we are certain that He, glory be to Him, distinguished some from others in wealth and poverty, and in the length and shortness of life, by a consummate wisdom whose true nature none comprehends except Him, so we likewise know that He made some differ from others in form and colour by a consummate wisdom. This is because through this difference the good-doer is distinguished from the evil-doer, and the близкий relative from the stranger. Then he said: "We bear witness, a testimony beyond doubt, that He, glory be to Him, did not differentiate between appearances and forms except when He knew the good of His servants in it, even if we do not know the precise good."

The third view: al-Wasiti said: "What is meant is the form of the obedient and the disobedient. So the one He fashioned in the form of loyalty is not like the one He fashioned in the form of enmity." Others said: "It is an indication of the purity of souls and their darkness." Al-Hasan said: "Among them is one whom He formed so as to take him exclusively for Himself, and among them is one whom He formed so as to occupy him with other than Him."

An example of the first: He created Adam so as to single him out with the subtleties of His kindness, to elevate his station, and He manifested his spirit from among His beauty and majesty. He crowned him with the crown of honour and adorned him with the mantle of majesty and awe.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 82, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, but you deny the Judgment (al-din)﴾. Know that when He, glorified is He, had explained by rational proofs the soundness of the statement about resurrection and rising again in general, He followed this with an explanation of the detailed circumstances related to that, and these are of several kinds.

The first kind: He, glorified is He, rebuked them for that delusion by His saying: "Nay" (kalla). "Bal" (but) is a particle laid down in the language to negate something that has already preceded, while something else has been established. Therefore, they have mentioned several interpretations of "kalla":

The first: al-Qadi said: its meaning is that you do not stay upright in acknowledging My blessings upon you and My guidance to you, but rather you deny the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din).

The second: "kalla," meaning: desist from being deluded by the generosity of God. Then it is as if He said: and you do not desist from that, but rather you deny the Judgment (al-din) altogether.

The third: al-Qaffal said: "kalla" means: the matter is not as you say, that there is no resurrection and no rising again, because that would entail that God Most High created creation in vain and aimlessly, and He is far exalted above that. Then it is as if He said: and you do not benefit from this clarification, but rather you deny. And in His saying: ﴿you deny the Judgment (al-din)﴾ there are two aspects.

The first: that by "al-din" is meant Islam, and the meaning is that you deny the recompense for the religion and Islam.

The second: that by "al-din" is meant the reckoning, and the meaning is that you deny the Day of Reckoning.

**The second type: His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders, who know what you do﴾.**

The meaning is an expression of wonder at their condition, as if He, glorified is He, said: You deny the Day of Judgment, which is the Day of Reckoning and Recompense, while the angels of God are assigned to you, recording your deeds so that you will be held accountable for them on the Day of Resurrection. A parallel to this is His statement: ﴿One sitting on the right and one on the left. He does not utter a word but that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18, 17], and His statement: ﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians﴾ [al-An'am: 61].

Then there are several discussions here.

**The first discussion:** Some people have objected to the presence of the Noble Recorders on several grounds.

One: these angels are either composed of subtle bodies, like air, breeze and fire, or of dense bodies. If the first is the case, their structure would necessarily be disrupted by the slightest cause, such as strong winds blowing or a hand, sleeve or whip passing through the air. If the second is the case, we must be able to see them, for if it were possible for them to be present while we do not see them, it would be possible for there to be suns, moons, elephants and trumpets in our presence which we neither see nor hear. That would be a denial of what is evident. The same applies to denying their pages, their selves and their pens.

Two: if this act of having them record is devoid of benefit, it is pointless, and that is impermissible for God, exalted is He. If it has a benefit, that benefit either returns to God, exalted is He, or to the servant.

The first is impossible, because He is exalted above benefit and harm. This makes clear the falsity of the view of those who say that He had them record only out of fear of forgetfulness and error.

The second is also impossible, because at most one can say that the benefit of this recording is that they will be witnesses against people and proof against them on the Day of Resurrection. But this benefit is weak, because a person who knows that God does not act unjustly or oppress does not need this proof in his case, and one who does not know this does not benefit from this proof, since it is possible that God commanded them to record those things against him unjustly.

Three: acts of the heart are neither visible nor perceptible, so they belong to the category of the unseen, and the unseen is known only to God, as He said: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. If these acts are not known to the angels, it is impossible for them to record them, yet the verse requires that they be recorders over us of everything we do, whether it be acts of the heart or not.

As for the answer to the first objection: this objection holds only according to our school, on the basis of two principles.

The first: bodily structure is not a condition for life according to us.

The second: when the sense faculty is sound, the perceived object is present, and all other conditions are fulfilled, perception is not obligatory. On the first principle, the angels may be subtle bodies that are torn and scattered, yet their life remains despite that. On the second principle, they may be dense bodies, but we do not see them.

As for the answer to the second objection: God has conducted His affairs with His servants according to how they deal with one another, because that is more effective in establishing the meaning for them. Since the most effective method among them for accountability is to produce a book with witnesses, they are addressed in the same manner regarding what they will be held accountable for on the Day of Resurrection. Books will be brought out for them, opened, and there will be angels present there who will testify against them, just as the sultan's trusted agents testify against one who disobeys him and opposes his command. They will say to him: The king gave you such-and-such and did such-and-such for you, then you abandoned him and did such-and-such. So it is here too, and God knows best the reality of that.

As for the answer to the third objection: the most that can be said is that this generality is specified to the acts of the limbs, and that is not impossible.

**The second discussion:** His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians﴾, although it is a direct address, the community is in agreement that this ruling is general regarding all the accountable. There are two possibilities here.

One: there is a group of guardians, and that group guards all the children of Adam without any single angel being specifically assigned to a single child of Adam.

The second: the one assigned to each of them is different from the one assigned to the other. Then it is possible that the one assigned to each child of Adam is a single angel, because He matched the plural with the plural, which requires matching the singular with the singular. It is also possible that the one assigned to each of them is a group of angels, as it has been said: two by night and two by day, or as it has been said: they are five.

**The third discussion:** He, exalted is He, described these angels with attributes:

First: that they are guardians.

Second: that they are noble.

Third: that they are recorders.

Fourth: that they know what you do, and this has two meanings.

One: they know those acts so that they are able to record them, and this is a reminder that a person may not give testimony except after knowledge.

**Type three of the ramifications of the question of the Resurrection is His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿Indeed, the righteous are in bliss﴾ ﴿And indeed, the wicked are in the Blazing Fire﴾ ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾ ﴿And they will never be absent from it﴾.

Know that when God, exalted is He, described the Noble Scribes who record the deeds of the servants, He mentioned the states of those who act, saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous are in bliss﴾, which is the bliss of Paradise, ﴿and indeed, the wicked are in the Blazing Fire﴾, which is the Fire. In this verse there are two issues.

They say: the one who commits a major sin is a wicked person (fājir), and all the wicked are in Hell, because the word "al-Jaḥīm" (the Blazing Fire), when preceded by the definite article *alif-lām*, conveys comprehensiveness (*istighrāq*, i.e., the inclusion of all instances). The discussion of this issue has been thoroughly examined in Surat al-Baqara, but here there are additional points that must be mentioned. The Wa'īdiyya (the Threateners, the Mu'tazilite-leaning school that holds the threat of punishment is absolute) said: this verse contains aspects that indicate the perpetuity of the threat.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾. The Day of Recompense is the Day of Judgment (*yawm al-jazā'*), and there is no time except that it enters into it, just as you say "the day of this world" and "the day of the Hereafter."

The second: al-Jubba'i (the Mu'tazilite theologian Abū 'Alī al-Jubbā'ī) said: if we restricted His saying, ﴿And indeed, the wicked are in the Blazing Fire﴾, then some of the wicked would attain Paradise, and if they attained it, they would be among the righteous. This would entail that the wicked are not distinguished from the righteous, and that is false, because God has distinguished between the two. Therefore, it is necessary that the wicked do not enter Paradise, just as the righteous do not enter the Fire.

The third: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will never be absent from it﴾, which is like His saying: ﴿They will not be people who come out of it﴾ [al-Mā'ida: 37]. If there is no death and no absence, then after these there remains only eternal abiding in the Fire, forever and ever. Since the term "al-fājir" (the wicked) includes the disbeliever and the Muslim who commits a major sin, it is established that the people of major sins will remain forever in the Fire, and it is established that intercession is for the obedient, not for the people of major sins.

The answer to this: we have demonstrated that the indication of general terms (*alfāẓ al-'umūm*) for comprehensiveness is a speculative (*ẓannī*), weak indication, and the matter (the question of the punishment of sinners) is a definitive matter (*qaṭ'iyya*). It is impermissible to rely on a speculative proof for a definitive objective. Rather, there is here what indicates our position: the use of the plural definite with *alif-lām* referring to a previously mentioned (*ma'hūd sābiq*) group is common in the language. Therefore, it is possible that the expression here refers back to the disbelievers who were mentioned earlier, namely those who deny the Day of Recompense. The discussion of this has already been presented in detail. We grant that generality indicates certainty, but we do not grant that the person who commits a major sin is a wicked person (*fājir*). Since this first division is invalid, the second remains, and that conveys restriction (*ḥaṣr*). The preference lies with this side, because their proof must encompass all the wicked at all times, otherwise their aim is not achieved, whereas our proof suffices for its validity by encompassing some of the wicked at some times. The fourth category: among the ramifications of the Resurrection is the magnification of the Day of Judgement, which is found in His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿Then, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿The Day when no soul will have power for another soul at all, and the command that Day belongs to God.﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: They differed concerning the address in His words "And what will make you know" (wa-ma adraka). Some said it is an address to the disbeliever, by way of rebuking him. Most of them said it is an address to the Messenger (ﷺ), and He addressed him in this way because he had no knowledge of it before revelation.

The second issue: The majority hold that the repetition in His words, ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿Then, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾, is for the magnification of that Day. Al-Jubba'i said: Rather, it serves a renewed benefit, since what is meant by the first is the people of the Fire, and what is meant by the second is the people of Paradise, as if He said: "And what will make you know what the wicked will be treated with on the Day of Recompense? Then, what will make you know what the righteous will be treated with on the Day of Recompense?" And He repeated "the Day of Recompense" to magnify what He does, may He be exalted, with regard to these two groups in both matters.

The third issue: Concerning ﴿The Day when no soul will have power﴾ (yawma la tamliku), there are two readings: the nominative (raf') and the accusative (nasb). As for the nominative, there are two views:

The first: that it is in apposition (badal) to "the Day of Recompense."

The second: that it is by implying "huwa" (it is), so the meaning is: "It is a Day when no soul will have power..."

As for the accusative, there are several views:

The first: by implying "yudanun" (they will be recompensed), because "al-din" (the Recompense) indicates it.

The second: by implying "udhkuru" (remember).

The third: what al-Zajjaj mentioned, that it may be in a position of nominative, but it is built on the fatha (vowel) because it is in construction (idafa) with His words "la tamliku" (will not have power). Whatever is put in construction with a non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) element may be built on the fatha, even if it is in a position of nominative or genitive, as in the verse:

Nothing prevented them from drinking except that a dove cooed in branches of the awqal tree,

so "ghayr" was built on the fatha when it was put in construction with His words "an naṭaqat" (that she cooed). Al-Wahidi said: What al-Zajjaj mentioned concerning building on the fatha is permissible only according to al-Khalil and Sibawayh, when the construction is with a past verb, such as your saying "'ala hina 'atabtu" (at the time when I rebuked). But with a future verb it is not permissible to build in their view, while it is permissible according to the Kufans. We have discussed this issue under His words: ﴿This is a Day on which the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 119].

The fourth: what Abu 'Ali mentioned, which is that since "al-yawm" (the Day) in most cases occurs as an adverb of time (zarf), it was left in the state of the majority. The evidence for this is the consensus of the reciters and the Arabs in His words: ﴿Among them are the righteous, and among them are others below that.﴾ [al-A'raf: 168], and no one reads it in the nominative. Among what strengthens the accusative is His words: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ ﴿The Day when people will be...﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 3–4], and His words: ﴿They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense?"﴾ ﴿The Day they will be tried over the Fire.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 12–13]. So the accusative in ﴿The Day when no soul will have power﴾ is like this.

The fourth issue: They held to His words ﴿The Day when no soul will have power for another soul at all﴾ in denying intercession for the sinners. It is like His, exalted be He, words: ﴿And guard yourselves against a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123]. The answer to this has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah.

The fifth issue: The people of this world used to gain dominion (yataghallabuna 'ala al-mulk), and some of them would help others in matters and protect one another. But when the Day of Resurrection comes, the dominion of the worldly rulers will vanish and their leadership will be removed, so no one will protect anyone, no one will suffice for anyone, and no one will prevail over a kingdom. Its parallel is His words: ﴿And the command that Day belongs to God﴾ and His words: ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense.﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4]. It is a great warning, in that He informed them that on that Day only righteousness and obedience will benefit them, apart from everything else that used to benefit them in this world, such as wealth, children, helpers and intercessors. Al-Wahidi said: The meaning is that God, exalted be He, did not grant anyone any authority over any matter on that Day, as He had granted them authority in the abode of this world. Al-Wasiti said: In His words ﴿The Day when no soul will have power for another soul at all﴾ there is an indication of the annihilation of everything other than God, the Exalted. There, messages, words and ends all perish. Whoever's attribute is like this in this world, his worldly life will be his hereafter.

As for His words ﴿And the command that Day belongs to God﴾, it is an indication that subsistence and existence belong to God, and the matter is thus in eternity, on that Day and in the Hereafter, and it has not changed from one state to another. The variation returns to the states of the observer, not to the states of the one observed. Thus the perfect ones do not vary in their states according to the variation of times, as one of them said: "Even if the veil were lifted, I would not increase in certainty." And like Harithah, when he was informed in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "It is as if I am looking, as if I were, as if I were." And God, glorified and exalted, knows best, and all praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.
